hgroup > p:first-child.description:
The `

` that opens a heading group, before its heading: an eyebrow, the short label above the heading, set in small capitals. A `

` after the heading, a subtitle, keeps the body's face.

.lede.description: The opening paragraph, set slightly larger.
.lede.example: One paragraph saying what this page decides.

.tag.description: An inline chip label. Add `ok`, `warn` or `danger` to draw it in that status tone.

.callout.description: An aside set off from the prose by a tint, for something the user must not miss. Add `ok`, `warn` or `danger` when it reports a status, as `class="callout warn"` for a paused release; the tint and the title take the tone, and the prose keeps the body's ink. The title is a `<strong>` written as the callout's first child; one opening a paragraph stays in the body's ink. In a flow wider than the column, such as a sidebar page's body, it keeps the prose width; one holding a wide chart or table takes `data-width`.
.callout.example: <aside class="callout" id="rollback-note">Rollback is one flag flip; the backfill is idempotent.</aside>

pre.terminal.description: A terminal session: each command a `<b>` holding its prompt, its output plain beneath it, an `<i>` on a line of its own where output was cut, and a `<mark>` on the part of the output the reader should notice. The command reads in bold and the cut in the code's muted ink, and long lines wrap rather than scroll sideways. Put it in a `<figure>` with an `id` and a `<figcaption>` that says what the run shows.

section.panel.description: A titled region on a sidebar page (`<main class="layout-sidebar">`) holding one thing, such as a table, a log or a list of steps, under a short heading that names it. The heading and spacing group the region without an enclosing card; its contents keep their own visual structure.

.facts.description: A grid of labels and values for summary facts, written as a definition list. As a direct child of an `lf-option` with a `label`, it floats right as a narrow column where the option is wide enough, so the options' figures line up.

.metric.description: A metric tile: one figure under the label that names it, with an optional change beside the figure in a `<small>`, written as a one-term definition list. A row of them goes in a `layout-tiles` block. It is set as type under a hairline rather than as a card; restyle it through the theme's tokens.
.metric.example:
open failures
2 change: -1
sample duration
4 min

td.num.description: A table cell holding a quantity, right-aligned so the figures in a column line up on their last digit. Put `class="num"` on the column's heading cell too, or the heading sits left of its figures. Add the class to each such cell yourself. Leaf doesn't infer it, since "60" and "60 sessions" look alike.
